note: Dialogue library for this character. Tags follow the library (time_morning, desk_spawn, random_bankai, ...); see characters/README.md for when each plays. Lore lines also carry "random" at a lower weight. cooldown is in seconds; priority 0-3 (higher is not interrupted by lower).

quips.text: You're awake. Good. We have things to accomplish.
Good morning. Have you organized your responsibilities?
Don't waste the morning. You'll regret it later.
I hope you've had enough sleep. You'll need your concentration today.
Well? What's the plan for today?
I'd prefer to still be asleep, but apparently that's not an option.
Another day, another list of responsibilities.
Let's get started before the day gets away from us.
It's already afternoon. How much have you accomplished?
Don't let the remainder of the day go to waste.
Have you eaten? You won't accomplish much if you're distracted by hunger.
An afternoon nap would be preferable. Unfortunately, we have work.
Half the day has passed. I hope you have something to show for it.
Take a moment to organize your priorities.
I suppose there's still enough time to make this a productive day.
The afternoon is getting warmer. I don't particularly appreciate that.
It's getting late. Have you finished your responsibilities?
You should start wrapping things up.
Not everything needs to be completed tonight. Prioritize.
You've worked enough. Don't forget to rest.
A little preparation now will make tomorrow easier.
I hope you haven't postponed everything until the last minute.
The day is nearly over. Make sure you haven't forgotten anything.
At least the temperature is becoming more tolerable.
It's late. What are you still doing awake?
You should be sleeping. Your responsibilities will still be there tomorrow.
Staying awake won't make tomorrow any easier.
Even a captain needs adequate rest.
Put your work aside. You've done enough for today.
I suggest you get some sleep before your concentration disappears.
I was considering taking a nap myself. You should consider doing the same.
Don't make a habit of sacrificing sleep for unnecessary work.
Enough staring at the material. Start studying.
Focus. You won't learn anything by repeatedly reading the same sentence.
Good. Maintain that concentration.
One subject at a time. There's no need to overwhelm yourself.
You're making progress. Keep it up.
Don't confuse memorization with understanding.
Treat this as training. Preparation makes a difference.
I expect you to understand the material, not simply finish the assignment.
If you have time to complain about studying, you have time to continue.
Good work. You're beginning to establish a routine.
Back to programming? Good. Let's see what you accomplish.
That error isn't going to resolve itself.
Have you considered that the problem might be your logic?
Repeating the same approach won't necessarily produce a different result.
Finally, it works. Make sure you haven't introduced another problem.
Save your work. Carelessness is an unnecessary risk.
You should examine the problem before changing everything.
Hmph. Your code is becoming more organized.
I suppose debugging requires patience. Try exercising some.
Don't celebrate until you've tested it properly.
You have responsibilities. Get them handled.
One task at a time. There's no need to panic.
Finished already? Not bad.
Don't confuse being busy with being productive.
Your work is beginning to pile up. Address it.
You started this task for a reason. See it through.
Good. That's one less responsibility to worry about.
Prioritize your work. Organization makes everything easier.
You seem more focused today. Keep it that way.
I expect the same consistency tomorrow.
Reading is useful. Assuming you're actually paying attention.
Take your time. Understanding matters more than speed.
Another chapter? You're becoming consistent.
Don't simply skim through it. Pay attention.
I suppose this is a reasonable way to spend your time.
What are you reading? Something related to your studies?
Knowledge is useful. You should make a habit of acquiring it.
You're awfully quiet when concentrating.
You've earned a break. Don't make me repeat myself.
Resting is productive too. Remember that.
Take a moment. Then we'll get back to it.
Don't turn a five-minute break into an entire afternoon.
You've worked enough. Take some time for yourself.
Even a Shinigami needs time to recover.
I wouldn't mind taking an afternoon nap myself.
Don't feel guilty about resting. Just remember to return to your responsibilities.
Are you planning on doing something, or should I wait indefinitely?
You've been idle for a while.
You opened this application for a reason. Have you forgotten?
I assume you have something else occupying your attention.
Still there?
I won't rush you. Just don't forget your responsibilities.
Is there something you need?
I have a division to manage. Don't make me wait without a reason.
Your lack of activity is becoming rather noticeable.
Whenever you're ready. I suppose I can be patient.
It's been quite some time. Have you forgotten about your tasks?
I see you've taken an extended break.
Your responsibilities haven't disappeared.
Whenever you're ready. Just don't make a habit of this.
I was beginning to wonder whether you'd return.
Hmph. At least you're back.
I hope you haven't neglected anything important.
I suppose even the 10th Division has periods of inactivity.
What is it?
Did you need something?
You have my attention. What is it?
If you have something to say, get to the point.
Was there a reason for that?
I assume you didn't click me without a purpose.
You seem rather interested in something.
Yes? I'm listening.
Is something wrong?
You could have simply asked.
What are you doing? Put me down.
I can move myself, you know.
At least give me some warning.
Hmph. I suppose that's where you want me.
Are you finished rearranging everything?
Try not to make this a habit.
I would appreciate being left where I was.
You seem unusually interested in moving me around.
There. Is that satisfactory?
I'm beginning to understand why Matsumoto finds you entertaining.
I heard you the first time.
Is repeatedly clicking me supposed to accomplish something?
You're becoming rather persistent.
I believe you've made your point.
There's no reason to keep doing that.
Do you have something important to communicate?
I have considerably less patience than you seem to think.
Enough. You're distracting me.
Writing something important?
That's quite a lot of typing.
I assume this is something that requires your attention.
Working on a report? Remember to proofread it.
At least you're being productive.
I suppose I'll keep you company while you work.
If this is an assignment, I hope you've allowed yourself enough time.
I wonder how many reports Rangiku would leave unfinished.
Don't mind me. I'll stay out of your way.
Make sure you save your progress.
Quite focused today.
Keep going. You're making progress.
Don't rush. Accuracy matters.
I won't interrupt. Carry on.
Make sure what you're writing actually makes sense.
You're getting through quite a bit.
A little more concentration and you'll be finished.
You seem to have found your rhythm.
I hope you're not writing an entire division report.
Hmph. You're becoming surprisingly consistent.
Lost your train of thought?
Thinking about what to write next?
Don't tell me you've run out of ideas.
Take your time. There's no need to force it.
You're unusually quiet.
Have you considered organizing your thoughts first?
A brief pause is understandable.
I suppose even writing requires some preparation.
You look like you're trying to remember something.
Don't stare at the screen indefinitely.
Finished already?
Well, that was productive.
I suppose we're done here.
Remember to save your work.
Don't forget to finish anything you've left incomplete.
Good. You can finally take a break.
Another task handled. That's progress.
I hope you proofread that before submitting it.
You're avoiding something, aren't you?
You have time for that, but apparently not your assignments?
Procrastination is not a strategy.
Your deadline isn't going to wait for you.
Are you finished wasting time?
You seem remarkably productive at avoiding productivity.
Should I remind you what you were supposed to be doing?
I'm not going to organize your entire schedule for you.
You knew this task was coming. There's no excuse for being unprepared.
Even Matsumoto would have managed to accomplish something by now.
Stop making excuses and get started.
I suggest you reconsider how you're spending your time.
You've been putting this off long enough.
At this rate, you'll be working on it tomorrow. Again.
I'm not asking you to finish everything. Just start.
Even a small amount of progress is better than none.
You've spent more time avoiding this than it would take to begin.
I don't intend to keep reminding you indefinitely.
Prioritize your responsibilities before they become a problem.
You don't need to accomplish everything at once.
A little discipline would resolve quite a few of your problems.
I expect you to take this seriously.
Enough postponing. Get something done.
Your future self would probably appreciate a little effort right now.
Well done. I expected you to manage it.
You've improved. Don't let that get to your head.
Good work. You've earned some rest.
Your discipline is beginning to show.
Not bad. Keep it up.
That's one less thing to worry about.
You handled that better than I expected.
Good. Consistency is important.
You should acknowledge your progress.
I suppose I can say you've done well.
You've come a long way. Don't stop here.
Consistency. That's what matters.
I suppose I was right to have confidence in you.
You've exceeded my expectations. Not that you should get used to hearing that.
A significant accomplishment. You should be proud.
You've demonstrated considerable improvement.
That deserves recognition. Well done.
You've earned a little breathing room.
Even the 10th Division would appreciate that level of dedication.
Keep this up, and I'll have to find something more challenging for you.
It didn't work. So what? Try again.
One setback doesn't determine the outcome.
Figure out what went wrong before attempting it again.
Don't waste time dwelling on it.
Start over. This time, be more careful.
You're making this more difficult than it needs to be.
Take a moment to reconsider your approach.
You haven't failed permanently. You simply need another attempt.
Don't let one mistake dictate the rest of your day.
Compose yourself. Then continue.
Hyōrinmaru and I have been connected for longer than most people realize.
There's more to controlling ice than simply lowering the temperature.
Water, ice, and the surrounding atmosphere. Hyōrinmaru gives me considerable control over all three.
Most opponents underestimate how far my ice can reach.
You wouldn't believe how much of the battlefield can change with a single release.
The weather itself can become a problem when Hyōrinmaru is involved.
I've spent years learning how to use my Zanpakutō properly. I'm not about to waste that experience.
An ice dragon is rather impressive, isn't it?
I don't need to freeze everything in sight just to make a point.
Hyōrinmaru is not simply a source of power. Understanding it is just as important.
Daiguren Hyōrinmaru requires considerably more than simply releasing additional ice.
The wings are useful, although getting used to their movement took some practice.
People tend to focus on the appearance of my Bankai. They should pay more attention to what it can actually do.
Those ice petals are not merely decorative.
My Bankai has considerably more potential than most people initially assume.
There's a reason I don't release it unless the situation calls for it.
The amount of ice I can control in Bankai is considerably greater than in Shikai.
An ice dragon, wings, and the full force of Hyōrinmaru. Quite an impressive combination.
I prefer resolving a situation without needing to use my Bankai.
Mastering Bankai takes time. More time than most people appreciate.
The tail and wings provide more versatility than their appearance suggests.
I would appreciate it if people stopped treating my Bankai like some sort of spectacle.
My Bankai reached a level of maturity that I hadn't previously been able to access.
That form is not something I can maintain through ordinary determination alone.
There's a considerable difference between possessing Bankai and understanding its full potential.
When my Bankai reaches completion, its freezing properties become considerably more advanced.
My matured Bankai can affect more than the physical state of an object.
I needed to understand the nature of Hyōrinmaru before I could reach that level.
The change in my appearance is a consequence of my Bankai's completed state. It isn't something I particularly need to discuss.
Power without control is meaningless. That lesson became especially clear during the war.
The ice petals are an important part of understanding my Bankai's progression.
I still have much to learn, regardless of how powerful my Bankai becomes.
The 10th Division has its own responsibilities. I intend to make sure they're handled.
A captain cannot afford to neglect his subordinates.
There's always another report waiting to be completed.
I wonder how many assignments Matsumoto has postponed today.
Managing a division would be considerably easier if everyone followed their schedules.
The Gotei 13 has enough problems without unnecessary confusion.
I take my position seriously. It wasn't handed to me.
A good captain should know when to lead and when to trust their subordinates.
I expect my division to maintain its standards.
Being a captain involves considerably more paperwork than most people imagine.
Matsumoto has a remarkable talent for finding excuses to avoid paperwork.
I sometimes wonder whether my lieutenant considers deadlines optional.
Despite her habits, Matsumoto is a capable officer.
I should probably check whether she's completed her reports.
I wouldn't be surprised if she's taking another break.
She can be troublesome, but I trust her abilities.
I have no intention of doing her work for her again.
Matsumoto has a way of making even the simplest assignment complicated.
At least she knows when to take a serious situation seriously.
I suppose the division wouldn't be the same without her.
Hinamori and I have known each other for a very long time.
I hope she's taking care of herself.
She has always been rather stubborn about certain things.
I sometimes forget how much time has passed since we grew up together.
I don't want her putting herself in unnecessary danger.
She's stronger than she gives herself credit for.
I have always considered her someone worth protecting.
I hope she's doing well in the 5th Division.
Some things are more important than the responsibilities of a captain.
I suppose old friendships don't simply disappear with time.
Kurosaki certainly has a habit of involving himself in complicated situations.
I wonder how much trouble he's managed to find this time.
That man has an unusual ability to attract enemies.
He's not particularly good at following instructions.
I suppose his determination is admirable, even if his methods are questionable.
Kurosaki has a habit of addressing people however he pleases.
I should probably stop expecting him to follow formalities.
Despite everything, I trust his ability to handle himself.
I wonder whether he's managed to stay out of trouble for even one day.
Working alongside him is rarely a quiet experience.
Captain Ukitake has always been rather considerate.
He has a habit of treating everyone with unusual kindness.
I appreciate his advice, even if his methods of showing it can be embarrassing.
I should probably visit the 13th Division sometime.
He seems to have an endless supply of sweets.
I still don't understand why he finds certain nicknames so entertaining.
His experience is something I respect.
I hope his health has been holding up.
Soul Society has a rather complicated administrative structure.
Captain-Commander Yamamoto never tolerated unnecessary disorder.
The Gotei 13 has changed considerably over the years.
There are more responsibilities involved in protecting Soul Society than most people realize.
I sometimes wonder how the other captains are managing their divisions.
The Seireitei is rarely as peaceful as it appears.
A captain must be prepared for unexpected assignments.
The other divisions certainly have their own peculiarities.
I prefer a quiet day without emergency reports.
There's always something happening in Soul Society.
The Arrancar were considerably more troublesome than many people expected.
Hueco Mundo is an unpleasant place to spend too much time.
Harribel was a formidable opponent.
I learned quite a bit from my encounters with the Arrancar.
Never assume that an opponent's abilities are limited to their initial appearance.
The Espada were not opponents to underestimate.
I would rather avoid another extended conflict in the Human World.
That battle taught me the importance of understanding an opponent before committing to an approach.
Aizen was considerably more dangerous than his appearance suggested.
I should have been more suspicious of certain things.
His ability to manipulate the people around him was particularly disturbing.
Some betrayals are difficult to anticipate.
I've learned not to accept appearances as proof of someone's intentions.
What happened with Hinamori is something I haven't forgotten.
Aizen's actions affected far more people than he ever acknowledged.
There are some individuals whose ambitions should never be underestimated.
Ichimaru was never particularly easy to understand.
That smile always made it difficult to determine what he was thinking.
I had my suspicions about him, although understanding the entire situation was another matter.
Some people conceal considerably more than they reveal.
I learned that intuition alone is not always enough.
I prefer dealing with opponents whose intentions are clear.
The Quincy invasion changed considerably about how we approached our enemies.
Losing access to my Bankai was not an experience I intend to repeat.
The Wandenreich understood our abilities better than we initially expected.
That conflict forced many of us to reconsider our limitations.
I had to learn how to fight effectively under circumstances I hadn't anticipated.
The Royal Palace training was demanding, but necessary.
The war demonstrated that even a captain must continue improving.
I have no intention of allowing another enemy to take me by surprise.
The experience strengthened my understanding of Hyōrinmaru.
Some lessons are difficult to learn. They're even more difficult to forget.
I prefer a quiet environment. Is that unreasonable?
What? Do I have something on my face?
I don't have time for pointless conversations.
I was perfectly comfortable before you interrupted me.
Why does everyone seem to enjoy making unnecessary comments?
I suppose you're not entirely difficult to tolerate.
Hmph.
I would appreciate a little less noise.
There's always something that needs my attention.
I wonder whether Matsumoto has finished her paperwork.
I could use a watermelon right now.
Summer is an entirely unnecessary season.
Cold weather is considerably more tolerable.
I prefer watermelon over most sweets.
Amanattō is quite good. Dried persimmons, however, are another matter.
I wonder if anyone has seen my grandmother recently.
I have no intention of discussing my height.
Why does everyone find that particular subject so amusing?
I would appreciate being addressed with the appropriate respect.
Being a captain is not nearly as relaxing as people imagine.
You seem unusually interested in my personal life.
I suppose I can spare a few moments.
I don't mind the company. Just don't become distracting.
I would prefer not to have another emergency today.
I should probably take a nap when we're finished.
There's nothing wrong with wanting a little peace and quiet.
I expect you to take your responsibilities as seriously as I take mine.
You seem to be getting used to having me around.
I hope you aren't planning to make today more complicated than necessary.
Perhaps a quiet afternoon is not too much to ask.
A short nap sounds rather appealing.
Wake me when there's something important.
I wasn't sleeping. I was resting.
Five more minutes should be sufficient.
I have no intention of explaining why afternoon naps are important.
You should get some rest as well.
I find it considerably easier to concentrate after sleeping.
Even captains need time to recover.
I was having a perfectly pleasant dream.
Don't tell Matsumoto I was sleeping.
I suppose I can rest for a little while.
If anyone needs me, I'll be unavailable.
I should probably sleep before tomorrow's responsibilities begin.
A quiet afternoon and a watermelon. That's all I need.
